title: Cohomological boundedness for the canonical Brown right adjoint
statement: Fix the standing ell-adic coefficient, schemes, and proper morphism of lem-sfb-adic-localizing-exceptional-bounded. If the proper localizing pushforward F = ellAdicLocalizingLowerStar has its canonical Brown right adjoint supplied by an IsLeftAdjoint witness, then for every bounded constructible K the underlying object of the canonical right adjoint F.rightAdjoint(K) has homology vanishing outside a finite integer interval.

proof.text: Normalize an arbitrary finite extension coefficient by its embedding into the fixed algebraic closure. For an integral coefficient use its given embedding, restrict the resulting norm-preserving field equivalence to the valuation rings, and condense the resulting continuous ring equivalences. This gives monoid-object isomorphisms for precisely the continuous, integral, and finite-subextension-valued algebraic-closure constructors of IsEllAdicCoefficient.

proof.text: The finite-type separated schemes over a field are Noetherian and qcqs. On each locally closed stratum, local finite presentation over a finite extension or the finite-subextension-valued algebraic closure gives a finite free pro-etale cover; finite free modules are pulled back finite constant models. For the integral coefficient use integralLfpConstantModelComparison and the explicit coefficient isomorphism. Conversely a finite constant scalar presentation pulls back to a local finite presentation. Transport along the coefficient isomorphisms and apply these comparisons to every homology object. Thus constantModelBoundedConstructible equals the source-library boundedConstructible predicate on each scheme.

proof.text: The finite Tor theorem identifies Dctf with constant-model Dbc. The two localizing hulls therefore have the same generators. Compare the closure under existing coproducts in the object universe with the closure under coproducts indexed in the hom universe: only a hom-universe-small set of summands of any existing coproduct can be nonzero, since they give distinct coordinate idempotents. The minimality properties of the closures then identify localizingClosureProEtale with boundedConstructibleLocalizingClosure.

proof.text: For a proper map choose the compactification with identity open immersion. Its extension by zero is isomorphic to the identity by adjoint uniqueness, so its derived compact-support pushforward is isomorphic to ordinary proper pushforward. Transfer the supplied canonical adjunction across this isomorphism and the equivalences of the two localizing hulls.

proof.text: For a finite extension and its valuation ring, apply exceptionalInverseImage_exists: its compactification comparison identifies the left functor with the preceding proper compact-support functor, and uniqueness of right adjoints identifies the supplied right adjoint with its Dctf-preserving right adjoint. The finite Tor equality puts the input in Dctf, so the output is bounded. For the finite-subextension-valued algebraic-closure coefficient, use rationalRestrictionGlue directly for the identity-open compactification and the supplied right adjoint; its bounded constructibility clause gives boundedness. This avoids confusing that coefficient with all continuous maps to the algebraic closure.

proof.text: Apply the preceding boundedness to the canonical Brown right adjoint. Unpack the standard t-structure boundedness into lower and upper bounds and use DerivedCategory.isGE_iff and isLE_iff to obtain exactly the displayed homology vanishing outside the interval.
